Why Does Apartment Cleanout in Toronto Depend So Much on the Building's Era?

c: Because few cities have this much genuine variety in rental and condo stock, and each type presents differently before a crew even reaches the unit. An older purpose-built rental tower from the sixties or seventies often has its own building superintendent and a more informal move-out process. A newer condo tower usually has strict booking rules for the freight elevator and a management office that needs a certificate of insurance in advance. A walk-up apartment might have no elevator at all, meaning every box and piece of furniture comes down the stairs by hand. Live Junk Free plans around whichever version is actually in front of the crew, rather than assuming one generic building type.
Converted house units — a Victorian split into two or three apartments — add their own layer, with narrower stairwells and doorways that need real care.
